introduction: On this fifth Sunday of Easter, the apostles choose seven men to serve at table, so that the needs of the widows are not neglected. In the Gospel, Jesus tells his troubled disciples, In my Father's house there are many dwelling places, and he says, I am the way, the truth and the life. Peter tells us that we are living stones, a royal priesthood, a holy nation. Let us follow Christ, our way to the Father.

prayerOfTheFaithful.invitation: Brothers and sisters, Christ is the way, the truth and the life. Let us bring our prayers to the Father through him.
intentions: For the Church: that all her members may use their gifts, as the apostles and the first deacons did, so that no one is neglected. Let us pray to the Lord.
For deacons: that they may serve God's people with faith and the wisdom of the Spirit. Let us pray to the Lord.
For widows, the elderly and all who are overlooked: that they may be cared for and valued. Let us pray to the Lord.
For those whose hearts are troubled: that they may trust in Jesus, who has prepared a place for them. Let us pray to the Lord.
For ourselves: that as living stones we may build up the Church and proclaim the praises of God. Let us pray to the Lord.
prayerOfTheFaithful.conclusion: God our Father, your Son is the way, the truth and the life. Keep us on the way that leads to you, and build us into a spiritual house for your glory. Through Christ our Lord.

reflection.title: The way, the truth and the life
reflection.body:
The early Church had growing pains. As the number of disciples increased, some complained that their widows "were neglected in the daily service." The apostles did not ignore the problem. They gathered the community and chose "seven men of good report, full of the Holy Spirit and of wisdom" to take care of the practical service, so that the apostles could continue "in prayer and in the ministry of the word." The Church has long seen in these seven, among them Stephen and Philip, the beginnings of the ministry of deacons. And the result was growth: "The word of God increased and the number of the disciples greatly multiplied."

In the Gospel, Jesus speaks to his disciples on the night before he dies. They are troubled, and he comforts them: "Don't let your heart be troubled. Believe in God. Believe also in me. In my Father's house are many homes." He promises to prepare a place for them and to come back for them.

Thomas speaks for all of us: "Lord, we don't know where you are going. How can we know the way?" Jesus answers: "I am the way, the truth, and the life. No one comes to the Father, except through me." Then Philip asks to see the Father, and Jesus says, "He who has seen me has seen the Father."

Peter tells us what we are becoming: "You also as living stones are built up as a spiritual house." And he describes our dignity: "you are a chosen race, a royal priesthood, a holy nation, a people for God's own possession."

This week, if your heart is troubled, bring it to Jesus and trust him. And look around your parish: is anyone being neglected? Use your gifts to serve them.
